625
The minutes of a Called meeting of the City Council.

Austin, Texas, May 05, 1890.
Hon. John McDonald, mayor presiding.

Roll Roll Call. Present. Aldermen Assmann, Jackson, Jones, Marchis, Nitschke, Phillips,
Dehnhein, Townsend, Zieer-9.
Call. Absent. Aldermen - Anderson, Baland, Carletan, Abraham, Hume, Linn, Mnitz, Newton,
North, Platt, Schneider, - 11.
There being no quorum present a Call of the Council was ordered.
Aldermen Anderson, Carletan, Linn, and North, entered the Council and the Call was
suspended.
The following Call was then read.
Call.               Austin, Texas, May 3, 1890.
To the members of the Council of the City of Austin.

Gentlemen: I hereby Call a
Special meeting of the City Council of the City of Austin to meet at the room of the
Council Monday morning May the 5th at 9 o'clock for the purpose of removing or accepting
the resignation of such election Judges heretofore appointed but who are unable or have
refused to serve and appointing in their stead such other persons as the Council may deem
proper to appoint.
John McDonald,
Mayor.
We the undersigned members of the City Council hereby accept service of notice of the
foregoing call for special meeting of the City Council this the 3d day of May 1890.
J.W. Morris, T. E.
Jones, C. E. Anderson, J. A. Jackson, A. A. Linn, J. H. F. North, George P. Assmann, J. H.
Graham, A. W.
Townsend, Fred Carletan, J. Linthcerne, J. W.
Nitschke, M. Boland, J. Schuler, A. H. Newton, Jno. W. Phillips, W. Zieler, C. S. Mnitz,
J. P. Dehneiden, R. Platt, [illegible] Alderman Zieler moved that as Chas. Caldwell


 --- Page break --- 

626
Judges would not accept the appointment of Judge of Election for the fourth Ward that Ed
Jurok be appointed in his stead. Carried.
Alderman Morris moved that as E. C. Bartholomew would not accept the appointment of Judge
of Election for the Third Ward that Jos. Harrell, Jr. be appointed in his stead. Adopted.
There being no objection, Alderman Scheider and Jackson were excused.
Notice having been received from the Judges of Election for the Eleventh Ward of the
appointment by them of G. D. Walker and J. B. Hutchison as Clerks as assistants, they were
confirmed as such Clerks as assistants.
Alderm Schneider entered the Council and
answered to his name.
John P. Kirk, was on motion, appointed Judge of Election for the Seventh Ward instead of
W. W. Archer who would not accept the appointment as Judge of Election for said Ward.
On motion, the Council then adjourned.
C. J Milton Morris,
City Clerk.
